name: JUSTICE WECHT
description: Concurred, argued that judges must curtail their First Amendment rights regarding partisan commentary while on the bench to maintain impartiality, distinguishing their speech from that of judicial candidates, but also noted that merely referencing past legislative deeds is not inherently transgressive if not done with a partisan tilt.

name: Wecht, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the average search engine user does not have an expectation of privacy in records generated by unprotected internet searches.

name: Chief Justice Todd
description: Concurred, argued that there was sufficient evidence of probable cause to support the issuance of the warrant.

name: JUSTICE MUNDY
description: Concurred, argued that sufficient probable cause existed for the warrant, making the constitutional privacy issue unnecessary to resolve, but noted agreement with the OAJC's view on privacy if it were necessary.

name: Stacy Wallace
description: Concurred, arguing that the Borough's Code provisions for administrative warrants without individualized probable cause violate the Pennsylvania Constitution's protection against unreasonable searches.

name: JUSTICE BROBSON
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court's order compelling arbitration does not meet the irreparability prong of the collateral order doctrine because the issue can be reviewed on appeal after a final judgment, and the limited standard of review for arbitration awards does not apply to trial court orders.

name: Justice McCaffery
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this matter.

name: WECHT, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that Section 3755 is facially unconstitutional as it mandates warrantless searches without a recognized exception.

name: MUNDY, JUSTICE
description: Dissented, argued that Section 3755 is not facially unconstitutional because it can be applied constitutionally with a warrant or exigent circumstances, and that the immunity provision in Section 3755(b) should be upheld.

name: BROBSON, JUSTICE
description: Dissented, argued that Section 3755 is not facially unconstitutional because it can be applied constitutionally if law enforcement obtains a warrant or if exigent circumstances exist, and that the statute is directed at medical professionals.

name: JUSTICE DOUGHERTY
description: Concurred, argued that the Commonwealth Court erred in denying Nonprofits' intervention because their environmental and health interests were not adequately represented by DEP, particularly regarding the Environmental Rights Amendment, and that the appeal from the preliminary injunction was moot.

name: TODD, C.J.
description: Concurred with the majority opinion and also joined Justice Donohue's concurring opinion.

name: DONOHUE
description: Concurred with the majority opinion and filed a separate concurring opinion.

name: MUNDY
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that the order denying intervention was not an appealable collateral order because Nonprofits' interests were adequately represented by DEP and their claim was not important enough or irreparably lost.

name: BROBSON, JJ.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that Nonprofits had no right to intervene in the RGGI Regulation case, that their environmental interests were fully vindicable through the legislative process, and that the "right" and "claim" prongs of the collateral order doctrine are coextensive.

name: JUSTICE DONOHUE
description: Dissented, argued that the Commonwealth failed to establish a high-crime area with objective evidence and that the designation was irrelevant to establishing reasonable suspicion for Lewis's seizure, thus the evidence should be suppressed.

name: Dougherty, J.
description: Concurred with the majority opinion, affirming the lower court's decision to deny suppression.

name: Justice Wecht
description: Concurred, arguing that mere presence among a group engaged in criminal activity, like gambling, could establish reasonable suspicion for each member of the group.

name: JUSTICE WECHT
description: Concurred in the result, argued that while the statute does not violate the Pennsylvania Constitution, the Majority's reasoning relies on an outdated and flawed "heightened rational basis test" (Gambone test) that encourages judicial overstepping, and the traditional rational basis test should have been applied.

name: JUSTICE BROBSON
description: Dissented, arguing that the Majority incorrectly broadened the Genser ruling to all disqualified mail ballots and mandated "notice and cure" procedures not supported by the Election Code or prior precedent, leading to non-uniform elections.

name: JUSTICE MUNDY
description: Concurred, argued that the Uniform Firearms Act requires PSP to provide background check results as quickly as possible with available resources and to make a good faith effort to keep the system staffed to minimize response times, and that declaratory relief is available to clarify these duties.

name: Chief Justice Todd
description: Dissented, argued that the practical utility of declaratory relief in this matter is questionable and that the appellants may be underwhelmed by it.

name: DONOHUE JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that Judge Braxton violated Section 17(a) by holding incompatible offices, creating a voidable conflict of duties that presumptively prejudiced the judicial actions, requiring vacation and remand, but rejected the automatic forfeiture rule.

name: Justice Mundy
description: Concurred, argued that the error was structural and resulted in presumed prejudice, but was subject to waiver.

name: JUSTICE BROBSON
description: Concurred, argued that the plaintiffs failed to state a legally cognizable claim that the firearm preemption laws are unconstitutional or otherwise infirm on the grounds of substantive due process, state-created danger doctrine, or interference with delegated public health duties.

name: JUSTICE MUNDY
description: Concurred, arguing that the grand jury report did not meet the statutory definition for public release and that due process requires all named but nonindicted individuals criticized in a grand jury report to be given notice and an opportunity to respond.

name: JUSTICE DONOHUE
description: Concurred, argued that the Election Code requires counting provisional ballots when a mail-in ballot is void, as this prevents double voting and upholds the right to vote.

name: JUSTICE MUNDY
description: Concurred, argued that the "proof is evident or presumption great" evidentiary limitation does not apply to the life-offense exception to the right to bail, meaning bail is categorically precluded for such charges.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE TODD
description: Authored the majority opinion, arguing that Articles of Impeachment became null and void upon the expiration of the 206th Session of the General Assembly because the General Assembly's powers last only for the duration of the session in which those bodies came into being.

name: WECHT
description: Concurred with majority opinion and filed a separate concurring opinion.

name: MUNDY
description: Filed a concurring and dissenting opinion.

name: DOUGHERTY
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this matter.

name: BROBSON
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this matter.

name: DOUGHERTY, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the Galapos' signs constituted protected pure speech and the injunction was an impermissible prior restraint under the Pennsylvania Constitution, as no substantial privacy interests were intolerably invaded.

name: WECHT, JUSTICE
description: Dissented, argued that the injunction was not a prior restraint and that equity courts can enjoin speech constituting a private nuisance, which the injunction in this case was.

name: BROBSON, JUSTICE
description: Dissented, argued that trial courts can enjoin residential speech that creates a private nuisance and disrupts quiet enjoyment, and that the injunction was content-neutral and narrowly tailored to protect residential privacy.

name: JUSTICE WECHT
description: Dissented, argued that inventory searches violate the Pennsylvania Constitution by depriving citizens of security in their possessions without adequate justification, and that the appeal should not have been dismissed as improvidently granted.

name: TODD CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, finding Appellee failed to prove SORNA's irrebuttable presumption unconstitutional and its requirements non-punitive.

name: Justice Mundy
description: Concurred, but disagreed that online registration requirements resemble shaming punishments, though ultimately agreed with the non-punitive finding.

name: Justice Wecht
description: Concurred on the irrebuttable presumption result but dissented on the finding that Subchapter H is not punitive, arguing it is punitive in effect.

name: Justice Donohue
description: Dissented, arguing the Majority's application of the irrebuttable presumption doctrine was flawed, SORNA's presumption unconstitutional, and its requirements punitive.

name: BROBSON, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the General Assembly never enacted a statute vesting the PUC with legislative authority over gas meter locations in historic districts, thus no unconstitutional delegation occurred.

name: JUSTICE DONOHUE
description: Concurred, argued that the Commonwealth Court lacked original jurisdiction because the Appellants' claims, though styled as challenging parole eligibility, fundamentally challenge the constitutionality of their life sentences without parole, which must be brought under the PCRA.

name: Justice Wecht
description: Dissented, argued that the majority incorrectly concluded that judgments of sentence prohibit parole and that parole ineligibility is part of the sentence, which he believes is not what the Crimes Code states and could hinder future legislative reforms.

name: The Late Chief Justice Baer
description: Did not participate in the decision of this matter.

name: Justice Brobson
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this matter.

name: WECHT, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the Receiver's actions were necessary and authorized by Act 47 to address the City's severe financial distress and local officials' mismanagement, and that Act 47 supersedes the City's Home Rule Charter.

name: Brobson, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Receiver's authority is to require and direct the municipality to implement the recovery plan, not to implement it independently, and would modify the plan accordingly.

name: Dougherty, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the challenged modifications are unlawful and arbitrary, exceeding the Receiver's statutory authority and impermissibly altering the City's form of government.

name: TODD, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that Act 12's legislative process satisfied constitutional requirements for original purpose and single subject, as all provisions related to benefits for low-income individuals and the title was not deceptive.

name: DOUGHERTY, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the "public health programs" provision in Act 12 fits the unifying subject of "benefits pertaining to the basic necessities of life to low-income individuals" because the funds are for medical assistance recipients.

name: MUNDY, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that Article III, Section 1, does not textually support a non-deception mandate for a bill's title, despite its inclusion in the court's test.

name: DONOHUE, JUSTICE
description: Dissented, argued that Act 12 violated both the "original purpose" and "single subject" rules, as the majority's broad unifying subject condones logrolling and undermines constitutional intent.

name: WECHT, JUSTICE
description: Dissented, argued that Act 12 violated the Pennsylvania Constitution because the court's inconsistent application of Article III rules undermines legislative transparency and condones practices like logrolling.

name: BAER, C.J.
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: BROBSON, J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this matter.

name: DONOHUE, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, arguing that the General Assembly intended to grant broad rulemaking authority to the Agencies, allowing them to define additional public resources consistent with the Environmental Rights Amendment, and that the challenged regulations are reasonable and do not violate the Documents Law.

name: DOUGHERTY, JUSTICE
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, agreeing the Agencies did not exceed power for "other critical communities" but would find they exceeded authority for "common areas of a school's property," "playground," and "playground owners" using ejusdem generis analysis.

name: WECHT, JUSTICE
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, agreeing with the reversal for most definitions but found a fatal procedural defect in the PNDI database's incorporation for "other critical communities," which he would affirm the Commonwealth Court's decision on.

name: MUNDY, JUSTICE
description: Dissented, arguing the Agencies exceeded their statutory authority in promulgating the challenged regulations and that the PNDI receipt violates the Documents Law.

name: BAER, C.J.
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: BROBSON, JUSTICE
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision.

name: Justice Donohue
description: Concurred, argued that the school district's selective property assessment appeal method violates the Uniformity Clause and that indefinite base year assessments lead to unconstitutional non-uniformity.

name: JUSTICE DOUGHERTY
description: Concurred, argued that the school district's methodology for choosing properties for reassessment is not neutral and is unreasonably discriminatory, violating the Uniformity Clause, and that the underlying problem of stagnant property values due to infrequent county-wide assessments requires a legislative remedy.

name: JUSTICE DONOHUE
description: Concurred, argued that Act 77's universal mail-in voting provisions do not violate the Pennsylvania Constitution, as the General Assembly has the authority to prescribe methods of voting.

name: JUSTICE WECHT
description: Concurred, except for the determination that Act 77 prescribed an "other method" of voting pursuant to Article VII, Section 4 of the Constitution.

name: JUSTICE MUNDY
description: Dissented, argued that the state Constitution, as historically understood and amended, requires in-person voting by default, and universal no-excuse mail-in balloting requires a constitutional amendment.

name: JUSTICE BROBSON
description: Dissented, joined Justice Mundy's opinion, arguing that the majority overrules 160 years of precedent without sufficient justification.

name: BAER, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that PEDF failed to prove the challenged provisions violate the Pennsylvania Constitution, as the use of funds for DCNR's operations and statewide environmental projects, and Lease Fund changes, align with trustee duties under the ERA.

name: SAYLOR
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this matter.

name: TODD
description: Concurred, joined the majority opinion and Justice Donohue's concurring opinion.

name: DONOHUE
description: Concurred, argued that while concerns exist about non-trust use of assets, the facial challenge fails, and detailed accounting will allow for future as-applied challenges.

name: DOUGHERTY
description: Dissented, argued that the challenged appropriations and fiscal code sections are facially unconstitutional for permitting non-trust use of funds and commingling without proper accounting, violating ERA trustee duties.

name: WECHT
description: Dissented, argued that the upheld legislation is facially unconstitutional due to allowing non-trust use of trust corpus and commingling without transparent accounting, similar to previously struck-down provisions.

name: MUNDY
description: Concurred, argued that the Commonwealth's allocation of oil and gas lease funds for broader trust purposes, beyond just remediation, is consistent with its trustee duties under the ERA.

name: JUSTICE MUNDY
description: Concurred, argued that the warrantless seizure of blood was unconstitutional because neither exigent circumstances nor Section 3755 justified it, and affirmed the Superior Court's suppression of evidence while vacating its constitutional ruling on Section 3755 as unnecessary.

name: JUSTICE WECHT
description: Concurred with the majority that exigent circumstances did not justify the warrantless seizure but dissented from the decision to vacate the Superior Court's constitutional ruling on Section 3755, arguing the statute's constitutionality should have been addressed.

name: DONOHUE
description: Concurred with the majority that exigent circumstances did not justify the warrantless seizure but dissented from the decision to vacate the Superior Court's constitutional ruling on Section 3755, arguing the statute's constitutionality should have been addressed.

name: DOUGHERTY
description: Concurred with the majority that exigent circumstances did not justify the warrantless seizure but dissented from the decision to vacate the Superior Court's constitutional ruling on Section 3755, arguing the statute's constitutionality should have been addressed.

name: TODD, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that Appellant's claims based on incorrect legal advice regarding the settlement's consequences are not barred by Muhammad, and her fraud claim can proceed.

name: SAYLOR, J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this matter.

name: WECHT, JUSTICE
description: Concurred in the result, but argued that the Muhammad precedent should be overturned entirely as it is deeply flawed and unjust.

name: MUNDY, JUSTICE
description: Concurred in the result, and agreed with Justice Wecht that the Muhammad rule should be disapproved and that the present dispute offers a convenient vehicle to do so.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE BAER
description: Concurred, argued that a Batson violation, while reprehensible and warranting a new trial, does not constitute the most egregious prosecutorial misconduct that would bar retrial under Pennsylvania's Double Jeopardy Clause, as it was not a tactic designed to provoke a mistrial or intentionally deprive the defendant of a fair trial.

name: Justice Mundy
description: Concurred, argued that the established remedy for a Batson violation has always been a new trial, and the expansion of double jeopardy protections in *Johnson* does not change this, as Batson violations are a distinct type of violation not to be commingled with other prosecutorial misconduct analyses for double jeopardy.

name: Justice Donohue
description: Dissented, argued that all Batson violations, as intentional acts of racial discrimination, inherently constitute prosecutorial overreaching that fundamentally breaks down the judicial process and should always result in the dismissal of charges (barring retrial) under Pennsylvania's Double Jeopardy Clause.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE BAER
description: Concurred, argued that the smell of marijuana alone is not sufficient to establish probable cause for a warrantless vehicle search, but can be a factor in the totality of circumstances.

name: Justice Saylor
description: Concurred, argued that the suppression court's ruling was based on expert testimony that the smell of legal and illegal marijuana is indistinguishable, and did not support broader pronouncements.

name: Justice Dougherty
description: Concurred that marijuana smell is a factor but not stand-alone probable cause, but dissented from reinstating the trial court's suppression order, arguing for remand to consider other factors.

name: Justice Mundy
description: Concurred that marijuana smell is a factor but not stand-alone probable cause, but dissented from the application of that holding to the facts, arguing the trial court overlooked relevant factors.

name: JUSTICE DONOHUE
description: Concurred, argued that DHS did not establish probable cause for a home inspection, violating Mother's Fourth Amendment and state constitutional rights.

name: JUSTICE DOUGHERTY
description: Concurred in the result that the juvenile court's order lacked sufficient basis, but dissented from the majority's analysis, viewing it as incongruous and potentially harmful to child welfare jurisprudence.

name: Justice Todd
description: Concurred in the result that the juvenile court's order lacked sufficient basis, but dissented from the majority's reasoning, viewing it as incongruous and potentially harmful to child welfare jurisprudence.

name: JUSTICE MUNDY
description: Dissented, argued that DHS established sufficient probable cause based on the totality of circumstances, including prior family involvement, to support the home visit.

name: JUSTICE WECHT
description: Concurred, argued that the 'proof is evident or presumption great' standard for denying bail is a unique standard, 'substantially more likely than not,' requiring a qualitative and quantitative assessment of evidence, and that screenshots were admissible duplicates under the best-evidence rule.

name: BAER, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the 'clear and convincing evidence' standard should apply for denying bail, as it is a well-known and workable definition, but ultimately concurred in the result.

name: TODD, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the 'clear and convincing evidence' standard should apply for denying bail, joining Chief Justice Baer's opinion.

name: MUNDY, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Majority's 'substantially more likely than not' standard for denying bail inappropriately heightens the Commonwealth's burden of proof and is contrary to precedent, but concurred in the ultimate outcome.

name: Justice Todd
description: Concurred, authored the majority opinion, arguing the Victim's Rights Amendment violated the separate vote requirement by combining multiple, non-interrelated changes that substantively altered existing constitutional provisions.

name: Justice Mundy
description: Dissented, arguing the proposed amendment was properly submitted as a single ballot question because its changes were narrowly tailored to a singular objective of victims' rights and did not substantively alter other existing constitutional provisions.

name: JUSTICE MUNDY
description: Concurred, argued that an order denying summary judgment based on sovereign immunity is a collateral order and thus immediately appealable, as sovereign immunity protects government entities from suit and this protection is irreparably lost if appellate review is postponed until final judgment.

name: DOUGHERTY
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this matter.

name: JUSTICE DONOHUE
description: Concurred, argued that bonus payments, rentals, and late fees are income but must be returned to the trust corpus because the ERA does not create income entitlements for beneficiaries.

name: BAER, C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that Section 27 should not be subject to intricate private trust principles but rather general trust concepts, and questioned whether the ERA was intended to govern income from natural resources.

name: SAYLOR, J.
description: Dissented, argued that applying private trust law principles to a public trust is incongruous and favored the narrowest application possible, affirming the Commonwealth Court's rationale.

name: WECHT
description: Concurred, argued that the ERA creates a trust where natural resources are the corpus, the Commonwealth is the trustee, and the people are beneficiaries, and revenue from trust asset sales cannot be redirected to the General Fund.

name: MUNDY
description: Concurred with the majority's analysis of bonus, rental, and late fees as income, but dissented on the analysis of Article I Section 27, aligning more closely with the Commonwealth Court's view.

name: JUSTICE WECHT
description: Concurred, argued that the sentencing statute is unconstitutionally vague because it fails to specify a maximum term, violating due process, and the judiciary cannot infer a maximum term.

name: SAYLOR, J.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that the sentencing statute is not unconstitutionally vague as a six-month maximum can be inferred from constitutional norms for summary offenses, and the judiciary should not declare it vague based on the majority's reasoning.

name: JUSTICE DONOHUE
description: Concurred, argued that the death penalty is constitutional and that Hairston's counsel was not ineffective regarding the verdict slip, prosecutorial conduct, or expert testimony.

name: JUSTICE SAYLOR
description: Concurred, expressed concerns about the prosecutor's use of misleading language regarding aggravating factors and the scope of expert testimony, but ultimately concurred in the result.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE SAYLOR
description: Concurred, argued that an unreasonably delayed license suspension, through no fault of the driver, can deny due process, and the driver demonstrated prejudice from the 28-month delay.

name: JUSTICE WECHT
description: Concurred in the judgment but dissented from the reasoning, argued that the Vehicle Code's statutory time limit for reporting convictions should be strictly enforced, making the suspension invalid without needing to invoke due process.

name: JUSTICE MUNDY
description: Dissented, argued that the Gingrich framework should be overruled, and the driver's own inaction contributed to the prejudice, making the suspension valid.
